assertions.name: hypB_prediction_is_q_squared_plus_q_minus_squared
assertions.source: sympy.simplify([4]_q/[2]_q − (q² + q⁻²)) with [4]_q = q³+q+q⁻¹+q⁻³ and [2]_q = q+q⁻¹; the Wenzl-projector chain tr_M(p_3) = [4]_q that the whole hypothesis rests on

assertions.name: classical_limits_match_known_values
assertions.source: |rung2(q=1) − 0| + |HypB(q=1) − 2| with measured rung2(q=1) = 0, HypB(q=1) = 2. The two limits differ, which is what makes the literal reading incompatible — a vanishing rung set equal to a non-vanishing one

assertions.name: hypB_literal_reading_confirmed
assertions.source: rung2 − HypB_pred = (-q**6 - q**4 + q**3 - 4*q**2 + 3*q - 2)/(q**4 + q**2), not identically zero, so Hyp-B in its literal reading is REFUTED

assertions.name: hypB_numeric_separation_at_q0
assertions.source: |rung2(q_0) − HypB(q_0)| = |0.000483716495696 − 2.04370621823|; the refutation is not a near-miss — the forms differ by a factor of ~4200 at the substrate

description: Definitive test of Hyp-B: does rung_2 = hbar_q^3/[2]_q equal tr_M(Wenzl p_3) / TL_loop = [4]_q/[2]_q? By Wenzl-projector identity tr_M(p_k) = [k+1]_q, the Hyp-B prediction = q^2 + q^-2 = -J_Hopf. Classical-limit cross-check independently confirms verdict.
